summary: Whatcom County, WA lakeside site: a 1933 L-5 cab and crows nest lookout, a 1942-43 Aircraft Warning Service post, removed or destroyed in 1959; footings remain.

facts.design: L-5 cab with a crows nest; WillhiteWeb says possibly a 35-foot tower added later
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1959 (the register and the Forest Lookouts page say removed; FireLookout.com says destroyed). Photo captions show an outhouse's remains and footings.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mt. Baker National Forest)

access.note: No trail reaches the site. It is reached on foot from the Ross Lake shore or from boating camps; a 2022 trip report describes a campsite for which the writer got a camping permit.

visit.trail_note: No trail to the site. Per WillhiteWeb, it is under a mile from the lake through forest that is easy walking.

events.note: Built with an L-5 cab and a crows nest; WillhiteWeb says a 35-foot tower may have been added later

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ on how the lookout ended in 1959: the register and the Forest Lookouts page say removed, FireLookout.com says destroyed, and WillhiteWeb says removed or destroyed. All agree on 1959.

notes_for_editor: The brief lists kind 'ground'; the sources describe an L-5 cab with a crows nest and possibly a 35-foot tower, so the kind may be wrong, but no source says it plainly. Left unchanged and flagged for review. The 'Zebra 1-9' designation on the weebly page could not be confirmed by a search; the story does not use it. Removal vs destruction in 1959 is the main conflict. The 2022 trip report is a personal account, used only for the current campsite and permit. No source found describes the site's remains in detail beyond photo captions. The weebly page lists the AWS dates under a 1943 report; the WebSearch summary of WillhiteWeb's AWS list was not checked. Access is set to public from the lake approach and the permitted campsite; no closure notice was found.
